To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) SNMP link loads and NetFlow records are "error correction codes", (2) using them together can improve traffic matrix estimation accuracy significantly, and (3) using dirty data (SNM and NetFlow errors) can contaminate traffic matrices, and identifying and cleaning them can improve estimation accuracy by orders of magnitude.

(1) SNMP link loads and NetFlow data are complementary to each other, and (2) SNMP link loads can serve as error correcting codes for NetFlow records, and (3) SNMP link loads should be used as a priori for traffic matrix estimation.

By combining SNMP link load measurements and sampled NetFlow measurements, we can improve the estimation accuracy of the traffic matrix by up to two orders of magnitude, even when sampled flow measurement are available at only 10% of the ingress routers."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions: How can we make use of multiple data source to improve estimation accuracy?
the following questions: (i) How to combine SNMP link load measurements and sampled NetFlow measurements to improve the accuracy of traffic matrix estimation?
the problem of traffic matrix estimation with dirty data, and we propose a novel approach to solve this problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is a significant advance in traffic matrix estimation.

, by using multiple information sources, we can estimate the traffic matrices with much higher accuracy and robustness, and therefore, the traffic matrix estimation problem is solved in a more practical manner.
, when the network topology is unknown, our algorithm can estimate the traffic matrix with an accuracy of 10%-20% of the true value, even when NetFlow data are not available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by using SNMP link loads and NetFlow records, the traffic matrices of the Internet backbone can be estimated much better than those obtained from either data source alone.
we show that the traffic matrix can be estimated much better with the combination of SNMP and NetFlow than either of them alone.
, by using multiple data sources, we can estimate traffic matrix more accurately than obtainable from any single information source alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SNMP link loads can serve as "check bits" to NetFlow records, and vice versa, and the combination of the two can be used to identify and remove errors.
SNMP link load and sampled NetFlow data are complementary, and they together can provide a robust and accurate solution for traffic matrix estimation, even with imperfect data.
, when full NetFlow is not deployed, it is important to collect link load measurements as well as sampled NetFlow data.
